clue.text: Clear-headed girls take lessons

indicators.note: '-headed' here means only the head, the first letter, of the word Clear is used

parts.note: lasses are girls

explanation.surface: Sensible young women attend their classes.
explanation.definitionFit: Classes are lessons, periods of teaching at school.

clue.text: Hooker finds a place to rest in animal shelter

indicators.note: 'in' says the resting place sits inside the shelter

parts.note: a cote is a shelter for doves or sheep
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A fisherman finds a bed in a dovecote.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocotte is an old word for a prostitute, which hooker is slang for.

clue.text: Win in a way despite being hostile

indicators.note: 'in' says the word for win goes inside a plus the road abbreviation

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
to gain is to win

explanation.surface: Victory achieved in a manner that is unfriendly.
explanation.definitionFit: To be against something is to be opposed or antagonistic to it.

clue.text: Not enough for a brief trip

parts.note: brief means short
a trip is a stumble or fall

explanation.surface: Too little time for a short holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortfall is a deficit, an amount by which supply falls below need.

clue.text: Minion dispatched to collect Rex and Virginia

indicators.note: 'to collect' says the word for dispatched gathers the other letters inside it

parts.note: dispatched means sent
R stands for Rex, Latin for king
VA is the US postal abbreviation for Virginia

explanation.surface: An underling is sent to pick up two people.
explanation.definitionFit: A servant is a lowly employee, a minion who does another's bidding.

clue.text: Various styles of capital

parts.note: 'capital' looks like a city or money, but it is the head, and its styles are the ways the hair on it is cut

explanation.definitionFit: Hairstyles are the arrangements given to the hair on one's head, the capital in its old sense.

clue.text: Gives practical experience?

explanation.surface: Someone passing on real-world training.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, hands on means passes along; hyphenated, hands-on means practical.
explanation.definitionFit: To hand something on is to pass it to another; hands-on work is direct practical involvement.

clue.text: Compound of nitre put in the ground

indicators.note: a compound mixes things together, so the letters of nitre are mixed

explanation.surface: A chemical compound of saltpetre is buried.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to bury, especially a dead body.

clue.text: Dared to include individual treated in godly style

indicators.note: 'to include' says the word for dared takes the letter inside it

parts.note: to defy is to dare or challenge
I is the Roman numeral one, an individual

explanation.surface: Someone bold enough to worship a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Deified means made into a god, worshipped as divine.

clue.text: Resilient band captured by foreign agent

indicators.note: 'captured by' says the band is held inside the agent

parts.note: a foreign agent is a spy
a ring is a band, as worn on a finger

explanation.surface: A tough gang is caught by an enemy operative.
explanation.definitionFit: Springy means elastic, bouncing back into shape.

clue.text: Claim I left what belongs to us in uproar

indicators.note: 'left' says the letter I has departed from the word Claim

parts.note: something that belongs to us is ours: our

explanation.surface: A protester stakes a claim during a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' takes I out of CLAIM to give CLAM; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A clamour is a loud outcry, an uproar.

clue.text: Talk about number one being comparatively dapper!

indicators.note: 'about' says the word for talk goes round the number one

parts.note: to natter is to chatter or talk idly
number one is oneself, I

explanation.surface: Gossip about who is the smartest dresser.
explanation.definitionFit: Nattier is the comparative of natty, meaning smart or spruce in dress.

clue.text: An article of faith — whichever way you look at it!

indicators.text: whichever way you look at it
indicators.note: reading from either end gives the same letters, so the answer is a palindrome

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A belief that holds true from every angle.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or doctrine held as true, a point of belief.

clue.text: Senator is about to make a statement

indicators.note: 'about' means scattered around, so the letters of Senator is are rearranged

explanation.surface: A senator is on the point of declaring something.
explanation.definitionFit: An assertion is a confident declaration, a firm statement of belief.

clue.text: Competitor, in the event, ran terribly well

indicators.note: 'in' says the answer sits inside the words that follow, running across them

explanation.surface: A competitor ran badly in the race, though it went well enough.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across evENT RAN Terribly; 'well' is a link word, added for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrant is someone who enters a contest, a competitor.

clue.text: Say you'll marry on saint's festival

explanation.surface: Agreeing to a wedding on a church holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is the phrase 'name the day', to fix a wedding date, run together as NAME DAY.
explanation.definitionFit: To name the day is to agree a wedding date; a name day is the feast of the saint one is named after.

clue.text: Intends banker to have income evaluation

parts.note: to mean is to intend
a banker is a river, something with banks; the Test is a river in Hampshire, southern England

explanation.surface: A financier plans to assess earnings.
explanation.definitionFit: A means test is an official inquiry into a person's earnings to decide eligibility for benefits.

clue.text: Determination to work things out afresh

explanation.surface: Making up one's mind to sort out problems once more.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits as RE-SOLVE, to solve again.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolve is firmness of purpose; re-solving is working a problem out a second time.

clue.text: Others admit Muhammad was a pragmatic man

indicators.note: 'admit' says the other word lets the boxer in

parts.note: the rest are the others
Muhammad Ali was the heavyweight boxer

explanation.surface: Others concede a boxer was practical.
explanation.definitionFit: A realist is someone who views things as they are, a practical person.

clue.text: Training session in airmen's mess

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so the letters are thrown about; it doubles as the airmen's dining room

explanation.surface: A course held in the RAF canteen.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminar is a class or meeting for discussion and instruction.

clue.text: It's clear I have been upset by depression

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the letters upside down, reading them backwards

parts.note: I have shortens to I've
a dent is a hollow, a depression

explanation.surface: Plainly I've been knocked back by feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns IVE into EVI; 'depression' looks like low mood but is a hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: Evident means plain to see, obvious.

clue.text: Hide article secreted by tragic king

indicators.note: something secreted by another is hidden inside it, so the article goes within the king

parts.note: King Lear is Shakespeare's tragic king
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean king hides a document.
explanation.definitionFit: Leather is tanned animal skin, a hide.

clue.text: Protracted obeisance to the victor of crécy?

parts.note: protracted means drawn out, long
a bow is a gesture of respect

explanation.surface: A deep bow to the winner of a famous battle.
explanation.walkthrough: English longbowmen won the battle of Crécy against France in 1346.
explanation.definitionFit: The English longbow is credited with winning the battle, so it is called the victor, by example.

clue.text: Leading lady takes drugs

parts.note: heroin is a drug
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A star actress takes narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: A heroine is the principal female character in a story.

clue.text: Artists harbour pile of swords

indicators.note: to harbour is to shelter, so the artists hold the pile inside

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist; RAS is the plural
a pier is a pillar or pile supporting a structure

explanation.surface: Painters keep a heap of blades.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapiers are slender thin-bladed swords for thrusting.

clue.text: Simon's aid somehow gains acknowledgment

indicators.note: 'somehow' says the letters arrive in some other order, an anagram

explanation.surface: A man named Simon gets help that earns recognition.
explanation.definitionFit: An admission is a confession, an acknowledgment that something is true.

clue.text: American cape made of fur

explanation.surface: A US cloak made of animal skin.
explanation.walkthrough: Cape Sable in Florida is the southernmost point of mainland USA; 'made of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Sable is a headland in Florida; sable is the prized pelt of a marten.

clue.text: Cancel the fight

explanation.surface: An order to call off a bout.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrap a plan is to abandon it; a scrap is also a scuffle or brawl.

clue.text: Being of humble origin, I belong elsewhere

indicators.note: 'elsewhere' says the letters of I belong are put somewhere else, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone of lowly birth feels out of place.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignoble in its old sense means of low birth, not noble.

clue.text: Direct route for column of workers

explanation.surface: The quickest path for a line of labourers.
explanation.walkthrough: Worker bees flying in single file form a BEE LINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A beeline is the straightest way to somewhere; a line of worker bees is a literal one.

clue.text: Men enter English river in spate

indicators.note: 'enter' says the men go inside the river's name

parts.note: the Trent is a major river in the English Midlands
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Soldiers wade into a flooded English river.
explanation.definitionFit: A torrent is a violent rushing flow of water, as a river in spate becomes.

clue.text: Dries up during hesitant speech?

parts.note: with can mean along with in time, as in 'wiser with age', so during
ers are the sounds of hesitant speech

explanation.surface: Someone stammering falls silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dries up' looks like forgetting one's lines, but it means shrivels.
explanation.definitionFit: To wither is to shrivel and dry out, as plants do in drought.
